Bhante, in 'web books meditations13 section0018 html 9394c5' (web books meditations13 section0018 html 9394c5), what is the core doctrinal teaching regarding 'The first thought that went through'?

In this section from *web books meditations13 section0018 html 9394c5*, the master explains: *"The first thought that went through his mind was, “Who’s looking after whom here?” But then he told himself that as long as he was awake, he should sit up and meditate."*. From the perspective of the Four Noble Truths, suffering arises whenever the mind grasps at impermanent phenomena (*anicca*) as a reliable self (*atta*). It is like grasping a poisonous cobra by the tail: tempting and sleek from afar, but deadly the moment you grasp it. Release the tail and live in safety. Anchor your understanding in direct seeing rather than speculative theory.
